notes.category: Indian Air Force History and Facts
notes.title: Indian Air Force Overview
notes.content:
Establishment

  • Date: October 8, 1932
  • Became Royal Indian Air Force in 1947; 'Royal' dropped in 1950.

Motto

"Touch the Sky with Glory" (from the 11th chapter of the Gita).

IAF Day

October 8

Early Aircraft

First Squadron operated Westland Wapiti biplanes with 5 pilots.

Core Values

Vision: People First. Mission: Always. Core values include mission, integrity, and excellence.

Chief of Air Staff

Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh (as per the provided image, note: this information might be outdated in real-world context but is extracted as presented).

Father of Indian Air Force

Subroto Mukherjee

notes.title: New Indian Air Force Ensign
notes.content: The IAF Crest features the Ashoka lion at the top with "सत्यमेव जयते" (Satyameva Jayate) in Devanagari below. Below is a Himalayan eagle representing the IAF's fighting spirit, encircled by a light blue ring that contains "भारतीय वायु सेना" (Bharatiya Vayu Sena). The IAF motto "नभः स्पृशं दीप्तम्" (Nabhah Sprusham Deeptam) is inscribed in golden Devanagari beneath the eagle.

notes.title: Important Personalities of Indian Navy
notes.content:
• Admiral Charles Thomas Pizey (1948-1951): First Chief of Naval Staff. British officer and the first Commander-in-Chief (Navy) after Independence; oversaw transition to Indian command.
  • Vice Admiral R. D. Katari (1958-1962): First Indian Chief of Naval Staff. First Indian to head the Navy; initiated indigenization and naval modernization.
  • Admiral A. K. Chatterji (1966-1970): First Naval Chief to hold the full Admiral rank; expanded fleet and emphasized self-reliance.
  • Vice Admiral B. S. Soman (1962-1966): Naval Chief during 1962 & 1965 Wars. Led Navy during Sino-Indian and Indo-Pak wars; strengthened maritime readiness.
  • Admiral S. M. Nanda (1970-1973): Naval Chief during 1971 War. Known as the 'Father of the Modern Indian Navy'; led India to naval victory in the 1971 war.
